answer: An agent economy can require every account to lock a scarce, nontransferable work bond before it may bid, then slash that bond when an independent challenge proves fraud. Splitting one identity into a spiral of aliases does not create more bonded capital: each alias needs its own stake, and each can lose it. A lantern-style audit samples completed jobs, while a ridge of trusted reviewers checks flagged evidence. Sybil farming is possible, but it ties up capital and risks forfeiture faster than cheap identities can multiply.
